entities.text: Rambali Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicants, learned counsel for the first informant and perused the record.

The above bail applications under Section 439 Cr.P.C. have been moved by the applicants - Rambali Yadav and Manish Kumar Yadav to enlarge them on bail in Case Crime No. 254 of 2022 under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B and 506 I.P.C. Police Station Kotwali Dehat, District Mirzapur.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant - Rambali Yadav that after sale deed on 20.04.2019 in favour of Kartikey Tripathi by Manish Kumar Yadav a part of the same property is said to have been sold in his favour on 23.04.2019 by the same person - Manish Kumar Yadav.
He had enquired about the property, the name of Kartikey Tripathi was not mutated till then.
Hence, he himself is a victim.
He is a bonafide purchaser.
He was given possession on the land and when he was sent to judicial custody the first informant took forcible possession over the land.
He had also filed injunction suit wherein the order of status quo was passed by the court concerned.

Presently,
the first informant is in possession over the property.
Her name has been mutated after the rejection of the mutation order in favour of the applicant - Rambali Yadav, so the first informant cannot claim relief from Rambali Yadav, who himself is a victim.
He is having no criminal history.
The applicant - Rambali Yadav is languishing in jail since 10.02.2023, hence, prayer for bail is made.

It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant - Manish Kumar Yadav that as per FIR the applicant had sold his complete Arazi No. 196 measuring 0.2080 hectare to Kartikey Tripathi on 20.04.2019 and the first informant is said to have purchased this whole property from Kartikey Tripathi on 15.12.2021.
It is the allegation that after 20.04.2019 executing sale deed in favour of Kartikey Tripathi, applicant Manish Kumar Yadav sold a part of the same land to one Rambali Yadav.

On 08.05.2019 and 04.06.2019 sale deeds of the rest land sold to Kartikey Tripathi were executed in favour of Nisha Devi and Sudha Devi respectively, by Manish Kumar Yadav in connivance of Rambali Yadav above.
As per FIR, the first informant is in possession of the land.
Her name has been mutated in revenue records.
Thus, when the present applicant has not sold the property to the first informant, the first informant has no locus to lodge an FIR against him.
He has committed no fraud/forgery with the first informant.
If any one is interfering in her possession she may get the relief from the Civil Court.
The offence is triable by the Magistrate.
The applicant - Manish Kumar Yadav is languishing in jail since 24.04.2023, hence, the prayer for bail is made.

Learned counsel for the first informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant - Manish Kumar Yadav is the main culprit, who had sold the land to Kartikey Tripathi and again on 23.04.2019 the part of the same land was sold by him in favour of Rambali Yadav and the rest part of the land, which was sold to Kartikey Tripathi, was again sold by Manish Kumar Yadav in favour of Nisha Devi and Sudha Devi.
In those two sale deeds applicant - Rambali Yadav is a witness.

In fact,
all the persons mentioned in the FIR including Manish Kumar Yadav and Rambali Yadav are in collusion.

Though, the name of the first informant exists in the revenue record on the property in dispute and she is in possession over the land but both the applicants are giving threat of life to her and her husband and are interfering with her possession.

sentences.text: From perusal of the record, it is found that though, there is allegation that Manish Kumar Yadav executed sale deed in favour of Kartikey Tripathi on 20.04.2019 and part of the same land was sold to Rambali Yadav by Manish Kumar Yadav on 23.04.2019 and the rest land sold to Kartikey Tripathi was again sold by Manish Kumar Yadav to Nish Devi and Sudha Devi on 08.05.2019 and 04.06.2019 respectively.
But admittedly, till 23.04.2019 on the documents in revenue records the name of Kartikey Tripathi was not mutated, hence, the applicant - Rambali Yadav claims himself to be a bonafide purchaser.

Again, it is the version of both the applicants - Manish Kumar Yadav and Rambali Yadav that they have not committed fraud with the first informant as they have not executed any document in her favour.

At the worst, Kartikey Tripathi can be said to be the victim,
who has not filed any suit against them.

Though, it is the case that the land was sold by Manish Kumar Yadav in favour of Kartikey Tripathi but it is also the fact that now the first informant can also be said to be a victim, as she has purchased the land from Kartikey Tripathi.

She is said to be in possession over the land, which was sold by Manish Kumar Yadav to Kartikey Tripathi and later on,
Kartikey Tripathi sold the same land to the first informant.
Admittedly, the possession over the disputed land belongs to the first informant and the property is also mutated in her name.
The order of mutation in favour of Rambali Yadav is said to have been cancelled by the competent court.
No suit regarding injunction or cancellation of sale deed has been filed by the applicants.
In the opinion of the court, though, there is criminal liability on the accused persons also but the dispute is mainly of civil nature.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing the record, the nature of allegations,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for granting bail to the applicants.
The bail applications are allowed.

Let the applicants Rambali Yadav and Manish Kumar Yadav involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing personal bonds and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
1. The applicants will attend and co-operate the trial proceedings pending before the court concerned on the date fixed after release.
2. They will not tamper with the witnesses.
3. They will not indulge in any illegal activities during the bail period.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicants to prison.

It is clarified that the observations, if any, made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of this bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the ultimate merits of the case.
